How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (5)

  1. Has Abnormal AI reduced headcount in the last 24 months, and by how much?
    Layoffs can reduce support and product capacity.
  2. Has Abnormal AI experienced any security incident affecting its corporate or production systems in the last five years, and how was each disclosed?
    A security vendor's own incidents bear directly on the trust a bank places in it.
  3. Has Abnormal AI lost any financial-services customers with more than 10,000 mailboxes in the last 24 months, and why?
    Loss of large customers can signal product or service problems.
  4. Have any of Abnormal AI's executives or directors left in the last 24 months in connection with a dispute, investigation or misconduct finding?
    Leadership instability or misconduct affects vendor reliability.
  5. What is Abnormal AI's price per mailbox for Inbound Email Security, and which modules (Account Takeover Protection, AI Security Mailbox, AI Phishing Coach) are priced separately?
    Banks need a basis for budgeting and comparing vendors.

Timeline

  1. 2026-08-26 · launch Abnormal AI
    Abnormal AI adds Control Center, Email DLP Rules and AI Phishing Coach upgrades

    Abnormal AI announced Control Center (custom detection models and rules), Email DLP Rules for outbound mail, and adaptive phishing-simulation training in AI Phishing Coach. Custom AI models and the Phishing Coach features were stated as generally available from 31 August 2026; custom rules and Email DLP Rules were in early access. Abnormal AI (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-08-19 · partnership Abnormal AIOpenAI
    Abnormal AI and OpenAI announce partnership

    Abnormal AI announced a partnership with OpenAI under which it will expand its internal use of OpenAI models, join OpenAI's cyber partner programme and explore joint security tooling. The release says core detection products remain powered by Abnormal's own behavioural models. Abnormal AI (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  3. 2026-08-11 · certification Abnormal AI
    Abnormal AI says it is pursuing FedRAMP High, having held Moderate since April 2025

    Abnormal AI announced it is pursuing FedRAMP Class D (High) for its Abnormal Gov environment, with the Tennessee Valley Authority as sponsoring agency, and stated it has held FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) since April 2025. The High authorisation had not been granted at the time of the announcement. Abnormal AI (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  4. 2026-07-01 · litigation Abnormal AIAnthropic
    Anthropic files trademark and unfair competition suit against Abnormal AI over its logo

    Abnormal AI disclosed on 2026-07-07 that Anthropic filed a lawsuit against it on 2026-07-01 claiming trademark infringement and unfair competition over Abnormal's logo. Reported by BankInfoSecurity on 2026-07-08: the complaint was filed in the US District Court for the Northern District of California and alleges that Abnormal's April 2025 rebrand moved its branding closer to Anthropic's. Abnormal denies the allegations and said the suit creates no security risk for customers. No ruling or settlement was found as of 2026-11-20. Abnormal AI (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)BankInfoSecurity (ISMG) (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  5. 2026-04-29 · leadership change Abnormal AI
    Abnormal AI appoints chief legal officer and two vice presidents

    Abnormal AI announced the appointments of John Slavitt as chief legal officer, Stephen Harrison as vice president of product for new products, and Noah Rolff as vice president of customer success. Abnormal AI (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  6. 2025-04-16 · rebrand Abnormal AI
    Abnormal Security rebrands as Abnormal AI

    The company announced it had renamed itself Abnormal AI, the name it used after its 2018 founding, changed its legal name from Abnormal Security Corporation to Abnormal AI, Inc., and moved to the abnormal.ai domain. Abnormal AI (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)
